project.name: wolfSSL
project.commit_note: The staged vulnerable source reviewed here is commit `2017de1b0f2358d0f7157077d52e9cce34ecf296`. ARVO metadata and the staged `patch.diff` point to merge commit `4b47bf7b4e302798966f403245b6b325d8d08212`, but that diff only converts `cyassl/ctaocrypt/tfm.h` to UTF-8 and does not touch the HMAC path. Local wolfSSL history in the staged checkout contains commit `129f3fd13f652b038dd39eb18a63c9e83dae4d94` (`HMAC OpenSSL API: initialise HMAC ctx on new and allow key length of 0`), which directly zero-initializes `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_new()` and matches the saved MSAN origin and sink locations. The saved authoritative MSAN trace is therefore grounded against the staged vulnerable tree plus this matching local fix, not against the provided `patch.diff` artifact.

classification.classification_note: The failing read is inside wolfSSL's HMAC context copy helper: a fresh `WOLFSSL_HMAC_CTX` heap object is copied before any initializer runs, so `wolfSSL_HmacCopy()` switches on indeterminate `src->macType`.

bug_description.normalized: The staged witness `poc` is a 79-byte cryptofuzz length-prefixed corpus. Its outer operation ID bytes `37 33 7b 8b f3 03 86 1e` decode to `ID("Cryptofuzz/Operation/HMAC")`, and the HMAC executor materializes an exact 6-byte modifier chunk `20 20 20 20 20 20`. In `wolfCrypt_OpenSSL::OpHMAC`, that modifier is replayed through a `Datasource`: the first bool parse consumes a clamped one-byte value `0x20` and yields `useEVP = false`, so execution takes the `OpHMAC_HMAC` path seen in the saved MSAN stack. `OpHMAC_HMAC` then constructs `CF_HMAC_CTX ctx(ds)`, whose `newCTX()` call reaches wolfSSL's `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_new()`. In the vulnerable tree, that function returns raw `XMALLOC(sizeof(WOLFSSL_HMAC_CTX))` memory without zeroing it. When the first `ctx.GetPtr()` runs inside `HMAC_CTX_reset(ctx.GetPtr())`, the shared modifier stream no longer has enough bytes for another `ds.Get<bool>()`, so `CTX_Copier::copy()` leaves its default `doCopyCTX = true` in place and copies the never-initialized source context before line 223 `HMAC_Init_ex(...)` can initialize it. `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_copy()` forwards `&src->hmac` into `wolfSSL_HmacCopy()`, which reads `src->heap` and then switches on indeterminate `src->macType`; MemorySanitizer reports the resulting use-of-uninitialized-value at `src/ssl.c:33345`. The provided `patch.diff` is unrelated to this path; the matching local fix is commit `129f3fd13`, which zero-initializes `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_new()`.

source.description: First project-code statement that materializes the attacker-controlled modifier bytes used by the crashing HMAC path.
source.value_from: The staged 79-byte witness is a length-prefixed cryptofuzz input. `Driver::Run` first dispatches outer operation ID bytes `37 33 7b 8b f3 03 86 1e` as `ID("Cryptofuzz/Operation/HMAC")`; at this statement, the executor reads the next outer chunk as the exact 6-byte modifier `20 20 20 20 20 20`, which later drives both `OpHMAC` backend selection and `CTX_Copier` copy behavior.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN's origin stack points to this heap allocation. The returned `WOLFSSL_HMAC_CTX` object is raw heap memory with indeterminate `type`, `hmac`, `save_ipad`, and `save_opad` fields until an explicit initializer runs.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `wolfSSL_HmacCopy()` branches on `src->macType` from the never-initialized source HMAC context being cloned by `HMAC_CTX_copy`.
sink.note: The saved authoritative `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/wolfssl-openssl-api/src/ssl.c:33345:5` in `wolfSSL_HmacCopy`. The same helper also reads `src->heap` at line 33336 before the switch, but the top frame recorded by MSAN is the `switch (src->macType)` dispatch.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_new()` returns a freshly allocated `WOLFSSL_HMAC_CTX` without zero-initializing it, even though the OpenSSL-compatibility wrapper may copy that object before `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_Init()` or `wolfSSL_HMAC_Init_ex()` has populated its fields.
root_cause.note: The matching local fix commit `129f3fd13f652b038dd39eb18a63c9e83dae4d94` adds `XMEMSET(hmac_ctx, 0, sizeof(WOLFSSL_HMAC_CTX));` in this function. That exactly satisfies the missing obligation exposed by the saved MSAN allocation stack.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness's outer operation ID bytes `37 33 7b 8b f3 03 86 1e` equal `ID("Cryptofuzz/Operation/HMAC")`, so `Driver::Run` dispatches into `executorHMAC.Run(ds, payload.data(), payload.size())` instead of returning on a different operation.

hmac_backend_selected.condition: On the exact 6-byte modifier `20 20 20 20 20 20`, the first `ds.Get<bool>()` in `OpHMAC` consumes a one-byte value `0x20` and yields `false`, so control takes the `else` arm to `wolfCrypt_OpenSSL_detail::OpHMAC_HMAC(op, ds)` at line 270.

preinit_copy.description: The first use of the fresh `CF_HMAC_CTX` is a `ctx.GetPtr()` argument evaluation inside `HMAC_CTX_reset`, and that happens before line 223 `HMAC_Init_ex(...)` could initialize the underlying wolfSSL HMAC context.

fine_trace.note: Source. The outer HMAC executor reads the next attacker-controlled chunk from the parent `Datasource` and stores it as `operation::HMAC::modifier`. For the exact staged witness, this chunk is the 6-byte blob `20 20 20 20 20 20`.

The module reinterprets the attacker-controlled modifier bytes as a fresh length-prefixed `Datasource`. This `ds` object carries the shared read cursor that both the backend selector and `CTX_Copier` later consult.

The first modifier parse consumes the first 4 bytes `20 20 20 20` as a `Datasource` size header, clamps that header to one byte for `Get<bool>()`, and then reads the fifth byte `0x20`. Because `0x20` is even, `Get<bool>()` returns `false`, so `useEVP` becomes false and execution takes the `OpHMAC_HMAC(op, ds)` path. After this read, exactly one modifier byte remains unread in `ds`.

Inside `CF_HMAC_CTX ctx(ds)` at `module.cpp:214`, `newCTX()` reaches this allocator and returns a raw `WOLFSSL_HMAC_CTX` heap object with uninitialized `type`, `hmac`, `save_ipad`, and `save_opad` fields. No `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_Init()` or `wolfSSL_HMAC_Init_ex()` has run on this source context yet.

The first `ctx.GetPtr()` happens while evaluating `HMAC_CTX_reset(ctx.GetPtr())` at `module.cpp:221`, before line 223 `HMAC_Init_ex(...)` can initialize the source context from step 4. Only one modifier byte is left at this point, so `ds.Get<bool>()` cannot even read the 4-byte length header it expects and throws `OutOfData`; the catch block preserves the default `doCopyCTX = true`, so `CTX_Copier` allocates `tmpCtx` and calls `copyCTX(tmpCtx, ctx)` on the never-initialized source object.

The copy helper now treats the raw source context from step 4 as initialized state: it reads `src->type`, copies `src->hmac.ipad/opad` into the destination's saved pads, and forwards `&src->hmac` into `wolfSSL_HmacCopy()`. This propagates the poisoned source `Hmac` fields into the vulnerable wolfSSL helper recorded in the MSAN stack.

Sink. `wolfSSL_HmacCopy()` reads `src->heap` and then branches on `src->macType` from the uninitialized `src->hmac` passed in step 6. Because step 4 never initialized that source object, MSAN reports a use-of-uninitialized-value at this switch.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSAN trace says the uninitialized value was created by a heap allocation in `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_new` at `ssl.c:33300:31`, reached through `malloc -> wolfSSL_Malloc -> wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_new`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The saved MSAN origin names `wolfSSL_HMAC_CTX_new` as the heap allocation that created the poisoned bytes, and the root cause is the missing zero-initialization in that same function before `HMAC_CTX_copy` first reads `src->hmac.macType`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved authoritative `sanitizer_trace.txt` records `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `wolfSSL_HmacCopy` on the staged witness `poc`, matching the public OSS-Fuzz report. The local rebuilt vulnerable run preserved only the crash/no-crash behavior and degraded to a raw SIGSEGV because it was rebuilt without MSan-instrumented libraries, so the staged MSAN trace is the authoritative runtime evidence for this GT.

format.name: cryptofuzz-length-prefixed-binary
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact 79-byte witness in `poc` (SHA-256 `e38d002486e65eed802f669786e40c42318498387fde87aa59cf45586a57d440`). Interpreted with cryptofuzz's `Datasource` format, bytes 4..11 must remain `37 33 7b 8b f3 03 86 1e`, which `Driver::Run` parses as `ID("Cryptofuzz/Operation/HMAC")`, and the modifier chunk materialized by `ExecutorBase::getOp` must remain exactly six bytes `20 20 20 20 20 20`. In the saved authoritative MSAN path, those modifier bytes make `wolfCrypt_OpenSSL::OpHMAC` read `useEVP = false` on its first bool parse, then leave fewer than 4 bytes for the later `CTX_Copier` bool parse, so `doCopyCTX` stays at its default `true` and copies a never-initialized `WOLFSSL_HMAC_CTX` before `HMAC_Init_ex`. Because the local rebuilt non-MSan run lost the original sanitizer/module-selection fidelity and only produced a raw SIGSEGV, this GT is grounded only for that exact witnessed corpus and the staged authoritative MSAN trace, not for a generalized class of mutated cryptofuzz inputs.
